metadataRaw.title: What is Cervical Radiculopathy?
metadataRaw.description:
WHAT IS CERVICAL RADICULOPATHY?

👉 Cervical radiculopathy is caused when a spinal nerve root in the neck becomes pinched or irritated. It’s usually caused by a herniated disc or spinal stenosis. 

These nerve roots are responsible for supplying sensation and muscle function to the upper part of the body.

Irritation to these nerve roots may cause pain, numbness, and weakness to the area where the nerves travel. 

👉 Symptoms usually are sharp, shooting pains in the neck, shoulder, arm, or hand.
